speaker: Unknown
en: Every time a new trillion dollar industry emerges, there's a need for this independent testing group.
zh: 每当一个新兴的万亿美元产业出现时，就需要这样一个独立的测试机构。

speaker: Unknown
en: When Meta released Llama 4 on our held out private benchmarks, the model was actually underperforming, but on all of the major public benchmarks, it was showing incredible capabilities.
zh: 当 Meta 发布 Llama 4 时，在我们留出的私有基准测试上，这个模型实际上表现不佳，但在所有主要的公开基准测试上，它却展现出了令人惊叹的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the limit of what you can achieve?
zh: 你所能达到的极限是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then within that, how are you going about it?
zh: 而在这其中，你打算如何实现？

speaker: Unknown
en: In an ideal world, take a frontier model and have it train the next version of itself, but obviously that's very expensive and slow.
zh: 在理想世界里，就是拿一个前沿模型，让它训练自己的下一个版本，但这显然非常昂贵且缓慢。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what we're doing is forming a set of proxies for every part of the process it takes to build the next version of the model.
zh: 所以我们在做的是为构建下一代模型所需的流程中的每一部分建立一组代理。

speaker: Unknown
en: Evaluations, as we become more complex, have a fewer sample size, but a larger set of criteria or expectations of them.
zh: 评估随着我们变得更复杂，样本量更少，但标准或对它们的期望集合更大。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where do you see the gap that's happening today?
zh: 你认为如今正在发生的差距在哪里？

speaker: Unknown
en: The government kind of has an inclination of what it's afraid of, be it biohacking or cyber hacking.
zh: 政府对它所害怕的东西多少有些倾向性认知，无论是生物黑客攻击还是网络黑客攻击。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then there becomes the question of, can the model do it?
zh: 但随之而来的问题是，模型能不能做到？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then can you get the model to do it?
zh: 然后是，你能不能让模型做到？

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you think the landscape will look like?
zh: 你认为这个格局会是什么样子？

speaker: Unknown
en: AI models keep getting better, but the tests we use to measure them can become obsolete almost as quickly.
zh: AI 模型不断变得更好，但我们用来衡量它们的测试几乎同样快地变得过时。

speaker: Unknown
en: In this episode, I'm joined by A16Z's Ben Horowitz and Jennifer Lee for a conversation with VAL's founder and CEO, Ryan Krishnath, about the increasingly difficult problem of measuring AI.
zh: 在这一集中，A16Z 的 Ben Horowitz 和 Jennifer Lee 与 VAL 的创始人兼 CEO Ryan Krishnath 进行对话，探讨衡量 AI 这个日益困难的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: We get into why public benchmarks can give a distorted picture of model capabilities, why independent evaluation matters, and what it takes to test a new model in a few hours before it launches.
zh: 我们会谈到为什么公开基准测试会给出模型能力的失真图景，为什么独立评估很重要，以及在新模型发布前几个小时内对其进行测试需要什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: But this is becoming about much more than model leaderboards.
zh: 但这正在变成远不止模型排行榜的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: As companies spend more on AI, they need to know which models and agents actually perform best for their own work and whether that intelligence is worth what they're paying for it.
zh: 随着公司在 AI 上的投入越来越多，它们需要知道哪些模型和智能体在它们自己的工作中真正表现最好，以及那种智能是否物有所值。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ryan also explains why benchmarks need to evolve alongside the models, how VALS is measuring recursive self-improvement, and why EVALS could eventually become a shared language for AI capabilities, risk, and policy.
zh: Ryan 还解释了为什么基准测试需要与模型同步演进，VALS 如何衡量递归自我改进，以及为什么 EVALS 最终可能成为 AI 能力、风险和政策的共同语言。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'll start a question from when VALS got started in 2024 after your team discovered that all the public benchmarks are just not sufficient enough to measure model progress and there needs to be a new methodology and approach coming to keep us on the frontier and help model labs continue to hill climb, take us back to the inception of VALS and what you see was missing in the market then.
zh: 那么我从一个问题开始，回到 VALS 在 2024 年创立之时，当时你的团队发现所有公开的基准测试都不足以衡量模型进展，需要一种新的方法论和方法来让我们保持在前沿，并帮助模型实验室继续爬山，带我们回到 VALS 的创立之初，以及你当时看到市场中缺失了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I mean, so I had a background doing research in particular building benchmarks and evaluations.
zh: 是的，我的背景是做研究，特别是构建基准测试和评估。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what was very clear to me was the very tight relationship between what it takes to build new systems for generation and actually new mechanisms for evaluation.
zh: 所以对我来说非常清楚的是，为新一代构建新系统与真正新的评估机制之间有着非常紧密的关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: In fact, in order to get one, you often need to get better at the other.
zh: 事实上，为了得到其中一个，你往往需要在另一个上做得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And actually one of the biggest drivers for model capability is having a new legible way to evaluate models.
zh: 而实际上，模型能力最大的驱动力之一，就是拥有一种新的清晰可读的方式来评估模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so around early 2024, what you're seeing is there are actually many interesting models coming to market.
zh: 所以在 2024 年初前后，你看到的是实际上有许多有趣的模型进入市场。

speaker: Unknown
en: They weren't all coming from OpenAI.
zh: 它们并不全都来自 OpenAI。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then also in particular, it was harder than ever to actually ascertain what was newly capable with the new models.
zh: 而且尤其是，要真正弄清楚这些新模型有什么新能力，比以往任何时候都更难。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so in kind of a first principles way, what we realized is that there would need to be some third party company that solely existed to build really high quality evaluations and benchmarks to be able to discern what was newly possible with these models.
zh: 所以以一种第一性原理的方式，我们意识到需要有一家纯粹存在的第三方公司，来构建真正高质量的评估和基准测试，以便能够辨别这些模型有哪些新的可能性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we released our first benchmarks in 2024.
zh: 所以我们在 2024 年发布了我们的第一批基准测试。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now over the last couple of years, that has kind of been realized by many different parts of the industry.
zh: 而在过去的几年里，这一点已经被行业的许多不同部分所认识到。

speaker: Unknown
en: I guess one of the obvious questions is why do you think the labs can't do this by themselves?
zh: 我想一个显而易见的问题是，你为什么认为实验室自己做不到这件事？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because they know the best of where the models are hill climbing on and what is missing capability-wise.
zh: 因为他们最清楚模型正在哪些方面爬山，以及能力上缺失了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why can't they be the benchmarking stores?
zh: 为什么他们不能成为基准测试的权威？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I mean, internally, they do build a lot of great benchmarks and that's what drives model progress.
zh: 是的，在内部，他们确实构建了很多很棒的基准测试，那正是驱动模型进步的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think there's an issue when we speak about model capabilities in a way that's self-reported.
zh: 但我认为当我们以一种自我报告的方式谈论模型能力时，是存在问题的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so one of the early indications of that you saw was when Meta released Llama 4.
zh: 你看到的早期迹象之一就是 Meta 发布 Llama 4 的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was a bit of a disaster.
zh: 那有点像是一场灾难。

speaker: Unknown
en: And interestingly, what we saw is that on our held out private benchmarks, the model is actually underperforming.
zh: 而有趣的是，我们看到在我们的留出私有基准测试上，这个模型实际上表现不佳。

speaker: Unknown
en: But on all of the major public benchmarks where the questions and rubrics are actually open source, it was showing incredible capability.
zh: 但在所有问题和评分标准都是开源的主要公开基准测试上，它却展现出了令人惊叹的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's a huge disconnect between what was self-reported based on these open benchmarks and then what we were actually finding with our higher quality, higher signal benchmarks.
zh: 所以在这些基于公开基准测试的自我报告，与我们用更高质量、更高信号的基准测试实际发现的结果之间，存在巨大的脱节。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think it speaks to a broader concept, which the labs, I think, understand that they would like to see a rational buying market.
zh: 但我认为这指向了一个更广泛的概念，实验室我想是理解的，他们希望看到一个理性的购买市场。

speaker: Unknown
en: They would like to see that when they invest billions of dollars to build a new model, there are actually substantive ways they can point to evidence and say, we're advancing in these ways.
zh: 他们希望看到，当他们投入数十亿美元构建一个新模型时，实际上有实质性的方式可以指向证据并说，我们正在这些方面取得进展。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's not just entirely self-reported to justify that investment.
zh: 而不是完全靠自我报告来证明那笔投资的合理性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you also see instances of Demis and others in the industry calling for an ecosystem of third party evaluators.
zh: 所以你也看到 Demis 和业内其他人在呼吁建立一个第三方评估者的生态系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what's the historical analog that you have in mind here?
zh: 那么你在这里想到的历史类比是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: There are rating agencies, audit firms.
zh: 有评级机构、审计公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the right comparable?
zh: 正确的类比是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think there's honestly lessons to learn across the board.
zh: 是的，我认为坦率地说，各方面都有值得学习的经验。

speaker: Unknown
en: And every time a new trillion dollar industry emerges, there's a need for this independent testing group.
zh: 每当一个新兴的万亿美元产业出现时，就需要这样一个独立的测试机构。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the fact that it's moved so quickly in AI has caused incestity for a lot of these parallels to be borne out.
zh: 而且 AI 领域发展得如此之快，我想正是这一点导致了许多这类平行关系以近亲繁殖式的方式呈现出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: We think about ourselves as trying to sit on both sides of the market.
zh: 我们把自己定位成试图坐在市场的两边。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there are mechanisms by which labs need to prove that new models are very capable, but there are also parallels where enterprises need to figure out what adoption strategies can amount to the greatest ROI for them.
zh: 所以一方面有机制需要实验室证明新模型非常强大,另一方面也有类似的情况,企业需要弄清楚什么样的采用策略能为它们带来最大的 ROI。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Take us through sort of the six-hour pre-release window before the model drops.
zh: 一家律师事务所里,associate 和 partner 之间的真正区别是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously, you need to run tens of billions of tokens without delaying the launch.
zh: 显然,你需要在不耽误发布的情况下跑数百亿个 token。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which part is you doing an all-nighter versus it being automated?
zh: 哪些部分是你在通宵干,哪些是自动化的?

speaker: Unknown
en: Take us through that.
zh: 带我们讲讲那个过程。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's honestly been a journey.
zh: 说实话这是一段历程。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the real goal, Northstar, we think about is we never want to be kind of a lagging indicator or a delay to a model release.
zh: 我认为真正的目标、北极星,是我们从来不想成为模型发布的一个滞后指标或延迟因素。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that means we have to move really, really quickly and extract the most possible signal with the rate limits or capacity that we have.
zh: 所以这意味着我们必须非常非常快地行动,用我们已有的速率限制或容量提取尽可能多的信号。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so early on, what this looked like was my co-founder Langston and I pulling an all-nighter to try and get as much done as possible and get results out the door.
zh: 早期的时候,这表现为我和我的联合创始人 Langston 通宵熬夜,尽可能多地完成工作,把结果交付出去。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now we built up a team, but we've also really invested heavily in infrastructure.
zh: 现在我们组建了团队,但我们也在基础设施上投入了巨资。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we're able to run evaluations in a massively distributed way, running effectively the maximum possible rate limits with every model we get access to.
zh: 所以我们能够以大规模分布式的方式运行评估,对我们能获得访问权限的每一个模型,实际上都用尽最大可能的速率限制。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we also have this internal system called Steve, Steve the Economic Vals employee.
zh: 我们还有一个内部系统叫 Steve,Steve the Economic Vals 员工。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's been a mechanism by which we're able to actually take more of the human work over time and put it into Steve.
zh: 这成为一种机制,让我们能够随着时间推移把更多人类的工作交给 Steve 来做。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you deal with the kind of issue that it's a little bit of an AI complete problem in that we still aren't really good at evaluating humans or we haven't agreed on it.
zh: 你怎么处理这样一个问题:这在某种程度上是一个 AI 完全问题,因为我们仍然不太擅长评估人类,或者我们还没有就此达成共识。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are things like IQ tests, there's EQ, there's the big five personality and so forth, but there's not really an agreed upon.
zh: 有 IQ 测试之类的东西,有 EQ,有大五人格等等,但并没有一个真正被公认的

speaker: Unknown
en: framework for which we do it.
zh: 框架来做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And people have issues with things like the SAT and this and that and the third.
zh: 人们对 SAT 之类的东西也有意见,这个那个的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then of course models are really good at hacking the benchmark.
zh: 而且当然,模型非常擅长破解基准测试。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so how do you think about that issue and what's the limit of what you can achieve?
zh: 那么你怎么看待这个问题,以及你能达到的极限是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: And then within that, how are you going about it?
zh: 在这个范围内,你们是怎么做的?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the honest answer is that it's forcing a lot of the more fuzzy or distributed forms of evals to be made explicit.
zh: 我认为诚实的回答是,它正在迫使很多更模糊或分散的评估形式被明确化。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is really the distinction between an associate and a partner at a law firm?
zh: 律师事务所里律师和合伙人的真正区别是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: And there isn't a clear test or an eval for that in the human world.
zh: 在人类世界里,并没有一个清晰的测试或评估来衡量这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we have to first establish a lot of that in these different enterprise or real world workflows for us to be able to test models in the same way.
zh: 所以我们必须先在这些不同的企业或真实世界工作流程中确立很多这样的标准,我们才能以同样的方式测试模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think long term, that will be actually the biggest bottleneck, our ability to take companies and their evals and make them legible, because that's how we'll figure out what signal we hill climb on and where we actually adopt.
zh: 我认为从长远来看,这实际上会是最大的瓶颈,即我们把这些公司及其评估变得清晰可读的能力,因为这就是我们确定在什么信号上进行爬山优化、以及真正在哪里采用的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Very interesting.
zh: 非常有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: Actually, maybe one question for you, Ben, on just like how the industry has formed before intelligence came through.
zh: 其实,也许问你一个问题,Ben,关于在智能出现之前这个行业是如何形成的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like we're now measuring something that's very fluid versus before, like when we're talking about enterprise software, there's Gartner rating on like 70 different metrics.
zh: 就像我们现在在衡量一个非常流动的东西,而以前,比如当我们谈论企业软件时,有 Gartner 对大约 70 个不同指标的评级。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like you can sort of stack rank on the quadrant to say this company has these features covered, these features not.
zh: 你可以在象限上做排名,说这家公司覆盖了这些功能,没覆盖那些功能。

speaker: Unknown
en: But now it's like very Jack Frontier that's very hard to measure given industries.
zh: 但现在就非常 Jack Frontier 了,在具体行业背景下很难衡量。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you see when is the analogy to the past that lessons we can borrow and what do you see that's really going to be the challenge and missing pieces going forward?
zh: 你看到了什么,与过去的类比有哪些可以借鉴的经验,你又看到什么将会是真正的挑战和未来缺失的部分?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a little bit reminiscent of the MPAA, right?
zh: 这有点让人想起 MPAA,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Where it's like, what's art?
zh: 就是,什么是艺术?

speaker: Unknown
en: What's porn?
zh: 什么是色情?

speaker: Unknown
en: Where's the line?
zh: 界限在哪里?

speaker: Unknown
en: When is it R?
zh: 什么时候是 R 级?

speaker: Unknown
en: When is it X?
zh: 什么时候是 X 级?

speaker: Unknown
en: And...
zh: 还有……

speaker: Unknown
en: By the way, the definition of that has changed over time, I think, things that used to be X are now R and so forth.
zh: 顺便说一下,这个定义是随时间变化的,我想,以前是 X 级的东西现在是 R 级,等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then what's PG-13, all that kind of thing.
zh: 还有什么是 PG-13,诸如此类。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there is no, in the famous line as well, I know when I see it and I think that this one, I just think it's going to be necessarily fuzzy, but there will develop norms over time.
zh: 正如那句名言所说的,没有确切定义,但我一看就知道。我觉得这一件事必然会是模糊的,但随着时间推移会形成规范。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, like if enough kind of
zh: 而且,你知道,如果足够多的

speaker: Unknown
en: People who run companies or run finance or run whatever it is kind of agree, yeah, no, that's a norm that I think it is, as opposed to kind of what we have a lot now in the open benchmarks, whereas if you can solve this specific problem, then you're at this level and so forth.
zh: 运营公司的人、运营金融的人或运营其他什么的人达成一致,对,那就是一条我认为成立的规范,而不是像我们现在在公开基准测试中有很多的那样,即如果你能解决这个具体问题,那你就处于这个水平,等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's one attackable and then it's too narrow.
zh: 我认为那样的东西既是可攻击的,又太狭窄了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think when you also look to some historic analogies, there's a lot of lessons that you can take from them as well on what's gone wrong and what we need to avoid.
zh: 我还认为,当你看向一些历史上的类似情况时,也能从中学到很多经验教训,关于哪里出了问题、我们需要避免什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think, for instance, at VALS, one very early decision we made was the decision to never sell training data to labs.
zh: 比如,我认为在 VALS,我们很早做的一个决定就是永远不向实验室出售训练数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's often a place that we're pushed.
zh: 这经常是我们被施压的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: When we start working with a new lab to actually source and sell for them a bunch of training data.
zh: 当我们开始与一家新实验室合作时,他们实际上想让我们为他们采购并出售大量训练数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, that's a lucrative business.
zh: 是的，那是一门很赚钱的生意。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And actually, a lot of that industry has now built these gimmick style benchmarks as a mechanism to sell their data.
zh: 而且实际上，那个行业里很多人现在已经构建了这些噱头式的基准测试，作为售卖他们数据的机制。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's become kind of their go to market as well.
zh: 所以这也变成了他们的一种进入市场的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think if you look at auditing as an industry, you end up with issues like Enron, where if you have the same group who's responsible for doing the audit, as well as also consulting and supporting the company, you have a mixed incentive structure.
zh: 但我认为，如果你把审计看作一个行业，你会遇到像安然公司那样的问题：如果同一个群体既负责做审计，又同时负责为该公司提供咨询和支持，你就会有一种混合的激励结构。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then it just becomes pay to pass the audit, or in this case, pay to win the benchmark.
zh: 然后这就变成了花钱通过审计，或者在这个场景下，就是花钱赢得基准测试。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's really not what the market benefits from and what we're trying to do.
zh: 而这真的不是市场能从中受益的东西，也不是我们想要做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Ryan, today you have already a pretty extensive catalog of different type of benchmarks.
zh: Ryan，今天你们已经有一个相当庞大的、不同类型基准测试的目录了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some of them are more focused on specific industries.
zh: 其中一些更专注于特定行业。

speaker: Unknown
